question.text: EURINR spot is 91.00. India's 6-month rate is 7% p.a. and Eurozone's 6-month rate is 3.5% p.a. What is the 6-month EURINR forward price?

explanation.text: The Logic: Using Interest Rate Parity, F = S x (1 + RQC x t) / (1 + RBC x t). Here EUR is the base currency (RBC = 3.5%) and INR is the quote currency (RQC = 7%). F = 91.00 x (1 + 0.07 x 0.5) / (1 + 0.035 x 0.5) = 91.00 x 1.035 / 1.0175 = 92.5651, which rounds to 92.57. The Trap: Swapping the rates and using 3.5% as RQC gives 89.43, which would imply EUR depreciating against INR even though Indian rates are higher than Eurozone rates. Note: Because Indian rates exceed Eurozone rates, EURINR futures trade at a premium to spot in line with IRP.
